The charm that untangles headphone cords and shoelaces on contact - that one took me eleven tries and one very burnt sleeve.
I made a salve that pulls a splinter out painlessly on its own. Nobody asked for it. Everybody needed it. That was kind of the whole philosophy.
Ink that never spills, no matter how hard you try to make it. I tried very, very hard.
I built a translation charm off a language that had been dead three hundred years before I ever touched it. Half the archives in the wizarding world run on it now, apparently.
There's a device the size of a coin that finds anything you've lost, as long as you loved it enough to miss it. I still think that's the best rule I ever wrote into a spell.
Weatherproofing for parchment. Not glamorous. Saved more essays than anything else I ever made.
I fixed the sock-matching problem. Nobody thanks you for that one, but everybody uses it.
The cure for never knowing your fly is unzipped - the one that got me out of the Tournament and into an actual career. Still the most requested thing I ever built.
A quill that never runs out mid-sentence. I built that one specifically because losing a good thought to a dry quill felt like a crime.
There's a small ward that softens thunder for kids who can't sleep through storms. That one wasn't for the industry. That one was just for me, a long time ago.
I once fixed a problem nobody had even named yet, just because I noticed it. That's the part people never understand about the small stuff - you have to actually be looking.
A hundred and thirty-eight patents, and not one of them was trying to change the world. I just wanted a Tuesday to be slightly less annoying to survive.
